findings.location: #s3-wizard, <div class="wizard-steps"> element wrapping three reordered .step divs, line 47
findings.evidence: DOM order: #s3-step3 (style="order:3") 'Confirm your order', then #s3-step2 (style="order:2") 'Enter payment details', then #s3-step1 (style="order:1") 'Choose a plan'
findings.violation: The three step divs' CSS order values (3, 2, 1) place them in the reverse of their DOM order, so a linearized reading encounters 'Confirm your order' before 'Enter payment details' or 'Choose a plan', reversing the actual decision sequence WCAG-1.3.2 requires to survive in markup order.
findings.fix: Reorder the three .step divs in the DOM to match the intended visual sequence (Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order) and remove or align the order values, so DOM order and visual order agree.

findings.location: #nav, <nav> element, the page's only navigation mechanism, line 11
findings.evidence: nav#nav contains exactly two links (Plan a trip, Service alerts); no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere in the document
findings.violation: The page relies solely on the primary navigation menu to reach other content, with no site search, sitemap, or breadcrumb trail offering a second, independent path, and the page is not one step in a linear process.
findings.fix: Add at least one independent wayfinding mechanism alongside the primary navigation, such as a site search form or a breadcrumb trail reflecting this page's place in the site.

findings.violation: This div wraps an icon-only, decoratively-marked image with no role, no accessible name, and no keyboard handler, so nothing in the markup exposes it as an interactive control at all.
findings.fix: Convert this to a native button element with a visible or aria-label describing the action (for example, 'Delete'), or add role="button", a text alternative, and a keyboard handler if it must remain a div.

findings.evidence: label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label>, the only one of the form's four labels (Route, Email address, Phone number, Promo code) carrying a color style
findings.violation: This label is distinguished from its three sibling labels by color alone, with no accompanying text, icon, or other non-color signal indicating why it differs.
findings.fix: Add a non-color signal alongside the red color, such as an asterisk plus a 'required' note or an inline icon with text, or remove the color difference if it carries no meaning.

findings.evidence:
Accessibility improvements

followed by paragraphs about mobile-app fare adjustments and calling rider services for real-time arrivals, with only one image (alt text) referencing accessible parking spaces
findings.violation: The heading promises accessibility improvements but the section's paragraph content describes fare adjustment and real-time arrival procedures unrelated to accessibility, so a reader scanning headings cannot predict what the section actually covers.
findings.fix: Retitle the heading to match its actual content (for example, 'Fares and real-time arrivals'), or move accessibility-specific content into the section and expand it so the heading matches what follows.

findings.violation: The error text for the invalid promo-code field reads only 'Error.', a generic placeholder that names neither the field nor what is wrong with the entered value.
findings.fix: Replace the error text with a specific message naming the field and the problem, for example 'Promo code not recognized. Check for typos or contact support.'
